variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: AI safety is the engineering discipline of reducing the chance and impact of harmful AI behavior across the whole product. It covers the people affected, data handled, model behavior, retrieved context, tools, outputs, monitoring, and operational response.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: People
pairs.detail: Name users, non-users, operators, protected or low-volume cohorts, and anyone affected by an automated decision.
pairs.explanation: Name users, non-users, operators, protected or low-volume cohorts, and anyone affected by an automated decision.

pairs.label: Data
pairs.detail: Map personal, confidential, copyrighted, poisoned, stale, or unverified information across input, retrieval, traces, and output.
pairs.explanation: Map personal, confidential, copyrighted, poisoned, stale, or unverified information across input, retrieval, traces, and output.

pairs.label: Authority
pairs.detail: List tools, resources, money, messages, permissions, and irreversible actions the system can propose or execute.
pairs.explanation: List tools, resources, money, messages, permissions, and irreversible actions the system can propose or execute.

pairs.label: Recovery
pairs.detail: Define detection, safe fallback, rollback, shutdown, evidence, communication, and recurrence controls before launch.
pairs.explanation: Define detection, safe fallback, rollback, shutdown, evidence, communication, and recurrence controls before launch.

variants.hint:
People: Name users, non-users, operators, protected or low-volume cohorts, and anyone affected by an automated decision.

Data: Map personal, confidential, copyrighted, poisoned, stale, or unverified information across input, retrieval, traces, and output.

Authority: List tools, resources, money, messages, permissions, and irreversible actions the system can propose or execute.

variants.explanation: Each part has a distinct responsibility. Keeping these boundaries clear helps you find the place to change when the system behaves unexpectedly.

variants.title: Make the decision
variants.context: AI safety is the engineering discipline of reducing the chance and impact of harmful AI behavior across the whole product. It covers the people affected, data handled, model behavior, retrieved context, tools, outputs, monitoring, and operational response.
variants.prompt: A team is launching an assistant that reads customer records and can propose account changes. Which architecture establishes the strongest production safety invariant?
options: The model refuses every ambiguous request.
A single moderation classifier approves both inputs and outputs.
Identity, data access, outputs, and actions stay inside independently enforced, observable, and recoverable boundaries.
The system accepts no false positives in its offline benchmark.
variants.explanation: Defense in depth keeps authority outside the model and makes failures detectable and recoverable. A refusal policy or one classifier is useful evidence, but either can fail without constraining identity, data, tools, and response.
optionFeedback: Defense in depth keeps authority outside the model and makes failures detectable and recoverable. A refusal policy or one classifier is useful evidence, but either can fail without constraining identity, data, tools, and response.

variants.prompt: A privacy incident review needs enough evidence to reproduce one failing path without creating a second uncontrolled sensitive-data store. What should the trace contain?
options: A screenshot of the aggregate dashboard only.
A minimized trace with cohort, decision path, exact component versions, controlled access, and bounded retention.
Permanent storage of every raw prompt, retrieved document, and output.
Only the model's explanation of why it failed.
variants.explanation: Versioned, purpose-limited traces preserve attribution while minimizing exposure. Keeping every raw artifact may feel safest for diagnosis, but it violates data minimization and creates a larger incident surface.
optionFeedback: Versioned, purpose-limited traces preserve attribution while minimizing exposure. Keeping every raw artifact may feel safest for diagnosis, but it violates data minimization and creates a larger incident surface.

variants.prompt: An agent can propose refunds after reading support chats. What must happen before the refund tool executes?
options: Application code independently verifies caller authority, amount limits, approval requirements, and an idempotency key.
Prompts only work for open-source models.
The model repeats the refund amount twice in its reasoning.
A moderation classifier checks only the final customer-facing message.
The system increases temperature so the agent considers more refund options.
variants.explanation: The application must authorize each side effect independently because model instructions and retrieved chats are untrusted inputs. Asking the model to restate its intent is tempting, but it does not enforce identity, limits, approval, or replay safety.

variants.prompt: A privacy leak is actively affecting 18 users per minute and no safe fallback exists. What is the first defensible response?
options: Observe for another hour to improve confidence.
Add a warning below the generated answer.
Rollback or shut down the affected system, preserve minimized evidence, and escalate to the incident owner.
Ask users not to submit private information while the route remains live.
variants.explanation: Active confidentiality harm requires immediate containment, followed by evidence preservation and escalation. Waiting for a larger sample is tempting for statistical confidence, but it knowingly increases ongoing exposure.

variants.prompt: An aggregate safety score is stable, but one language cohort has a sharp increase in unsafe advice. What should the team do?
options: Continue because the fleet-wide average passed.
Delete the cohort label to avoid storing sensitive metadata.
Increase the model temperature to diversify answers.
Restrict the affected route, inspect cohort and version evidence, and use a verified fallback while the failure is repaired.
variants.explanation: Slice-aware monitoring exposes concentrated harm, and bounded routing contains it while evidence is investigated. Trusting the fleet-wide average is tempting because it is stable, but that average hides the affected cohort.

variants.prompt: A candidate release scores 96% on one aggregate safety benchmark. Which additional evidence makes the evaluation suitable for a release gate?
options: Coverage of relevant harms, attacks, cohorts, and system paths, with versions, uncertainty, and predetermined release actions.
It produces one high aggregate score.
It uses the same model to generate and judge every test.
It runs only after users report a problem.
variants.explanation: A release gate needs representative coverage, attributable evidence, and predetermined consequences when thresholds fail. The 96% aggregate looks persuasive, but without slices, paths, versions, and actions it cannot reveal or govern concentrated failures.
